texts.preamble: Aparna Sen vs Rana Sen on 25 April, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Sheetal Chaudhary Pradhan Additional Sessions Judge-02, South-East District Saket Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal No. 233/2024 Ps- Sarita Vihar U/Sec. 29 Pwdv Act In the matter of :- Rana Sen S/o Late Sh. Saktimoy Sen Catering Manager, Air India Air India Catering, Igi Airport Terminal Ii Ifsd, New Delhi- 110037 .... Appellant Versus Aparna Sen W/o Sh. Rana Sen D/o Sh. Ramendu Das Gupta Office Address :- Sub Divisional Engineer (Ol) Bsnl Corporate Office Bharat Sanchar Bhavan, Hc Mathur Lane Janpath, New Delhi- 110001 .... Respondent Date of Institution : 19.07.2024 Date of Final Arguments : 16.04.2025 Date of Decision : 25.04.2025 Decision : [LEAKAGE_MASK].
texts.facts: This is an appeal U/Sec. 29 of the Protection Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred to as 'DV Act') against the impugned order dated 30.03.2024 (hereinafter referred to as 'impugned order') passed by Ld. Trial Court in CT Case No. 1737/2022 titled as "Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen". 2. Vide impugned order, Ld. Trial Court has directed the appellant/ husband herein to pay maintenance to the complainant to the tune of Rs. 15,000/- to be paid on or before 5th day of each Aparna Sen vs Rana Sen on 25 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141157385/ 1 English Calender month from the date of filing of the application u/sec. 12 of the Act till its disposal. 3. Appellant herein is the respondent/ husband and respondent herein is the complainant/ wife before Ld. Trial Court. In order to avoid any confusion, both the parties shall be referred with the same nomenclature with which they were referred before the Ld. Trial Court, in my subsequent paragraphs. 4. As per record of Ld. Trial Court, the brief facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, are as follows :- "The complainant (Aparna Sen) got a service in DoT as Junior Hindi Translator at Indore, MP in the year 1992. It has been stated that complainant (Aparna Sen) and respondent (Rana Sen) got married as per Hindu rites and ceremonies on 15.07.1994. Out of the said wedlock, two sons namely Satyajit and CA No. 233/2024 Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen Page no. 2 of 14 Shubhojit were born in the year 1996 and 2002 respectively. That respondent is a short tempered aggressive person and is over controlling, violent and by habit is a smoker and regular drinker. That respondent used to beat the complainant in front of her son besides causing heinous sexual abuse and mental torture at drunken state since marriage. The barbaric nature of the respondent did not spare his younger son either resulting in slapping his younger son and throwing hot food on his face filling his tender eyes and nostrils causing burning sensation. That respondent started doing regular chats with various women all through and used to meet them and do adultery, extra marital affairs. Further, that the respondent ill treated the complainant since her marriage with the respondent on 15.07.1994. Also that in the year 2018, the mother-in-law of the complainant had asked the complainant to leave the matrimonial house. However, currently, complainant is residing in the matrimonial house on a separate floor. However, the respondent is not co-habiting with the complainant. Further, that life of complainant is at high risk being a victim of violent abuse inflicted by respondent/ husband on regular basis. That respondent is demolishing the sanctity of complainant who is honest hard and working woman and a caring mother to her sons. That respondent though has sufficient income, property capacity to earn but has intentionally and deliberately failed, neglected and refused to maintain complainant. After being continuously harassed, abused and beaten for a long period, complainant forced to take legal help. Hence, the present complaint case". CA No. 233/2024 Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen Page no. 3 of 14 5. During the course of trial, income affidavits as directed by Ld. Trial Court were furnished by both the parties and matter was fixed for arguments on the application for interim maintenance moved by the complainant. 6. Thereafter, upon the application for seeking maintenance moved by complainant, Ld. Trial Court vide order dated 30.03.2024 directed the respondent/ husband to pay maintenance to the Aparna Sen vs Rana Sen on 25 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141157385/ 2 complainant to the tune of Rs. 15,000/- to be paid on or before 5th day of each English Calender month from the date of filing of the application u/sec. 12 of the Act till its disposal. 7. Feeling aggrieved by aforesaid impugned order dated 30.03.2024 passed by Ld. Trial Court, respondent/ husband has challenged the said order by way of present appeal by taking following grounds :- a) That respondent/ husband has retired now from active service. b) That respondent does not have any regular source of steady income as he is not receiving any pension. c) That in such type of financial conditions, it is difficult for respondent to maintain himself and his old aged mother who is dependent upon him. d) That respondent is suffering from chronic hyper disease and old age ailments. CA No. 233/2024 Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen Page no. 4 of 14 8.
texts.arguments: In addition to the above grounds, Ld. Counsel for respondent/ husband has argued that complainant is presently working in Bharat Sanchar Nigam, Limited and is getting handsome salary. It has also been argued that impugned order is vitiated by fatal infirmities and it prayed that impugned order passed by Ld. Trial Court, must be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 9. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the complainant has argued that impugned order passed by Ld. Trial Court, is legally correct and needs no interference and has been passed after considering the records of this case. Where a woman is subjected to cruelty by her husband or her relatives for demand of dowry, it is an offence u/sec. 498A of the Indian Penal Code. Keeping these CA No. 233/2024 Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen Page no. 5 of 14 objects and reasons in mind to provide for more effective protection of the rights of the woman guaranteed under Constitution who are victims of violence of any kind occurring within the family and for matter connected therewith or incidental thereto, the Bill was presented and the Protection of Woman From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 was passed by the Parliament. 12. The Act inter-alia provides for more effective protection or the right of woman guaranteed under the constitution who are victims of the domestic violence of any kind occurring within the shared household. According to the Act, any harm, injury to health, safety, life, limb or well being or any other act or threatening or coercion etc. by any adult member of the family, constitutes domestic violence. Further, the act also contemplates that any woman who is or has been in a domestic relationship, if she is subjected to any domestic violence can file a complaint u/sec. 12 of the PWDV Act. This Act also covers those CA No. 233/2024 Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen Page no. 6 of 14 woman who are or have been in relationship with the abuser where both parties have live together in a shared household and a relative by consanguinity, marriage or through a relationship in the nature of marriage or adoption. 14. For computing the maintenance, the following test have been laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Jasbir Kaur Sehgal vs. District Judge, Dehradun & Ors. 1997 (7) SCC 7, wherein it has been observed that: "No set formula can be laid for fixing the amount of maintenance. It has, in the very nature of things, to depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. Some scope for leverage can, however, be always there. The court has to consider the status of the parties, their CA No. 233/2024 Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen Page no. 7 of 14 respective needs, the capacity of the husband to pay having regard to his reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he is obliged under the law and statutory but involuntary payments or deductions. The amount of maintenance fixed for the wife or children should be such as she can live in reasonable comfort considering her status and the mode of life she was used to when she lived with her husband and also that she does not feel handicapped in the prosecution of her case. At the same time, the amount so fixed cannot be excessive or extortionate." 15. Further, Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr, Crl. Appeal No. 730/2020 (arising out of SLP (Crl) No. 9503/2018, dated 04.11.2020 has held as under :- Aparna Sen vs Rana Sen on 25 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141157385/ 4 Criteria for determining quantum of maintenance :- The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. There is no straitjacket formula for fixing the quantum of maintenance to be awarded. The factors which would weigh with the Court inter alia are the status of the parties; reasonable needs of the wife and dependent children; whether the applicant is educated and professionally qualified; whether the applicant has any independent source of income; whether the income is sufficient to enable her to maintain the same standard of living as she was accustomed to in her matrimonial home; whether the applicant was employed prior to her marriage; CA No. 233/2024 Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen Page no. 8 of 14 whether she was working during the subsistence of the marriage; whether the wife was required to sacrifice her employment opportunities for nurturing the family, child rearing, and looking after adult members of the family; reasonable costs of litigation for a nonworking wife. 16. Besides that, the court must take into consideration the status of the parties and the capacity of the spouse to pay for her or her child or his support, the financial capacity of the husband, his actual income, reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and dependent family members including his own child, whom he is obliged to maintain under the law, liabilities if any, would be required to be taken into consideration. The Court must have due regard to the standard of living of the husband, as well as the spiraling inflation rates and high costs of living. Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr (Supra) has held as under :- (c) Where wife is earning some income. The Courts have held that if the wife is earning, it cannot operate as a bar from being awarded maintenance by the husband. The Courts have provided guidance on this issue in the following judgments. Aparna Sen vs Rana Sen on 25 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141157385/ 5 19. Further, in order to determine the quantum of maintenance payable to an applicant, the Court shall take into account the criteria enumerated in Part B - III of the judgment Rajnesh Vs Neha and Anr. (supra). CA No. 233/2024 Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen Page no. 10 of 14 20. Under section 20 DV Act, the magistrate has powers to direct husband to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence and such relief may inter alia include the maintenance for aggrieved person as well as her children. 21. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case law titled as Dr. Kulbhushan Kunwar v. Raj Kumari (1970) 3 SCC 129, has held, which as under :- "12. Section 125 Cr.P.C. stipulates that if any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain his wife, his legitimate or illegitimate minor child, who are otherwise unable to maintain themselves, shall be obligated to do so. A moral duty and a statutory obligation is cast upon the husband to maintain his wife, minor children, parents who otherwise are not capable of maintaining themselves. 22. The onus is on the husband to establish with necessary material that there are sufficient grounds to show that he is unable to maintain the family and discharge his legal obligations for reasons beyond his control. The wife CA No. 233/2024 Aparna Sen Vs. Rana Sen Page no. 11 of 14 is also entitled to enjoy the same amenities as she would have been entitled to in her matrimonial home. Reliance in this regard is placed upon the case law titled as Nidhi Sudan Vs. Manish Kumar Khanna, 2023 SCC Online Del 7652. 23.
